# runr_api_key (Resource)

An API key of a consumer ([API keys](https://runr.sh/docs/api-product/#api-keys)): callers of `key` routes send it as `X-Api-Key` or `Authorization: Bearer`. The key itself (`key`) is in the answer that creates it and nowhere else: Terraform keeps it in the state (sensitive), so keep the state safe or hand the key on at once. Name, scopes, plan and expiry change in place; the key stays.

Destroying the resource revokes the key (callers get 401 within the region's sync interval). A key revoked outside Terraform is dropped from the state and created again. Rotation is an action, not a setting: `runr gateway keys rotate` makes a new key with an overlap; the resource then follows the new key (its `key` is not in the state; the command printed it).

Import with `<consumer id>/<key id>`; an imported key has no `key` (RunR never shows it again).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A key of Acme for GET and POST on /orders, valid until the end of 2027.
resource "runr_api_key" "acme_production" {
  consumer_id = runr_api_consumer.acme.id
  name        = "production"
  scopes = [
    { route_id = runr_gateway_route.orders.id, methods = ["GET", "POST"] },
  ]
  expires_at = "2028-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}

# The key is shown only when it is created: hand it to the consumer, e.g. into a secret store.
# Rotate it with `runr gateway keys rotate <key id> --overlap 1440`; the resource follows the
# new key (its key is not in the state then).
output "acme_key" {
  value     = runr_api_key.acme_production.key
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `consumer_id` (String) Consumer id (`runr_api_consumer`). Changing it creates a new key.
- `name` (String) Name of the key, e.g. `production`.

### Optional

- `expires_at` (String) When the key stops working (RFC 3339, e.g. `2027-01-01T00:00:00Z`; in the future when it is set). Left out: never. An expired key stays in the state (`status = "expired"`) until the time changes.
- `plan_id` (String) A plan for this key instead of the consumer's (`runr_api_plan`): its limits are counted for the key alone.
- `scopes` (Attributes List) Routes (and methods) the key may call: routes of the consumer's gateway (any gateway of the organization for an organization consumer). Left out: every route the consumer may call. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scopes))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Key id.
- `key` (String, Sensitive) The key (`rk_…`), known only from its creation; null after an import or a rotation outside Terraform.
- `prefix` (String) The key's first 11 characters, which tell keys apart.
- `status` (String) `active` or `expired`.

<a id="nestedatt--scopes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scopes`

Required:

- `route_id` (String) Route id (`runr_gateway_route`).

Optional:

- `methods` (Set of String) Methods on the route (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`). Left out: every method.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <consumer id>/<key id> (`runr gateway keys ls <consumer id>`); the key itself is not imported
terraform import runr_api_key.acme_production 01JCONSUMER0123456789ABCDE/01JKEY0123456789ABCDEFGHJK
```
